chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a man who was killed in a village or near a village that the people of that village are to bear the liability if no clear proof is found for the people of that village that they did not kill him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person is found killed in or near a village and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a person found killed in or near a village when the killer is unknown. It establishes communal financial liability upon the people of that village unless evidence is produced clearing them of responsibility, reflecting principles of judicial procedure and protection of blood-rights.
